entries.subject: DAMIT 5924: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-5924.txt. Model 5924, version 2021-11-12, pole (121°, -27°), period 9.29759 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 93 ±3 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021)
entries.finding: [Vernazza et al. (2021)](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/references/view/660) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the selected archive model has a physical size calibration. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 87.47 ± 1.13 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 63 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model publication supporting DAMIT 5924
entries.finding: The live DAMIT model-to-reference export binds selected model 5924 to VLT/SPHERE imaging survey of the largest main-belt asteroids: Final results and synthesis (2021). That publication supports the selected reconstruction. The imported entry conflated three surveys; listing them together did not establish three usable models or a registered reflectance mosaic.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 140, pole ['120', '-15'], [Model 140](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/140) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 140: pole (120°, -15°), 9.29759 h, version 2011-03-28, archive diameter 90 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 5 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 132 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.20 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.54; 0 of 5 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. The lens stands on the silhouette registration recorded in the entry above and on the route proven against the Dawn mosaic on Vesta; this test adds no independent check for this body. Removed on 2026-09-16: a lens ships only when every registration measurement that reaches a verdict places it within three degrees, and this one measured outline systematic 1.93° against relief −8.00°.
entries.revisitWhen: Registration measurements that agree within three degrees: a map, resolved markings, or a rotation record and mesh on which the outline and the relief place these frames together.
